maya: Noticed a spike in warmstart OOMs on fjord13b-int4 canary (hp-12) after traffic ramp.
maya: OOMs look like KV rehydration during multi-turn sessions. small prompts but long histories.

maya: sample log:
```
[2026-03-22T22:04:12Z] OOM allocating 980MiB for kv_cache shard=1
model=fjord13b-int4 host=hp-12 slot=1 prefetch=12 max_new_tokens=768
trace: kv_cache.rebuild -> alloc_slab -> memcpy -> OOM
```

devon: is prefetch high on these hosts? 12 sounds aggressive.
maya: yes, default prefetch 12 for this model in canary. also max_new_tokens set to 768.

sam: quick mitigation ideas:
- drop prefetch to 3 for canary workers
- reduce max_new_tokens to 256 by default
- enable soft_reserve + slab_compact_on_evict
- route >2k token sessions to highmem pool

aya: ran a short local sim with prefetch=3 + max_new_tokens=256, microbatch 4. result: peak kv alloc down ~60% and slab fragmentation lower.

maya: created small patch to model defaults and started rolling to 2/3 canary hosts.
ops-bot: deploybot: rolling update 6191230000 -> fjord13b-int4 defaults patch started. dashboard: https://console.redwood/models/fjord13b/canaries/6191230000

devon: monitor kv_alloc_peak, slab_frag_pct, and OOM_rate. set alert if kv_alloc_peak > 850MiB or slab_frag_pct > 30%.

aya: quick A/B after patch for 45m: OOMs v1=10.2% -> v2=0.6%. p95 latency 110ms -> 88ms. no regressions on our 500 prompt sanity set.
sam: note: longer rollup test (>3k tokens) shows truncation when max_new_tokens=256; quality delta small but visible for very long summaries.

maya: plan: keep patch on canary for 24h, run targeted eval on long-rollup set, and if OK promote. ticket created: INFRA-3429. PR: #842.

devon: follow-up: add runtime metric kv_rebuild_ops/sec and an internal gauge for active_prefetch_windows to help triage.
maya: thanks — will update the ticket and move to dedicated canaries after 24h if metrics stable. :thumbsup:
